task_objective: Prioritize three same-day tasks with different durations when a two-hour analysis has a hard 5 PM deadline.
constraints: Account for task duration rather than ranking solely by shortest task.

rius.description: Identify the two-hour analysis and its 5 PM deadline as the schedule's hard constraint.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if the analysis deadline/duration materially drives the ordering.
rius.rationale: Missing the fixed deadline could make an otherwise efficient sequence fail.

rius.description: Reserve enough uninterrupted time to complete the analysis before 5 PM, including reasonable buffer if current time permits.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if the plan explicitly protects a two-hour block before the deadline.
rius.rationale: The longest time-sensitive task requires capacity planning.

rius.description: Place the 15-minute email and 45-minute review around the protected analysis block based on urgency or coordination needs.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if the shorter tasks are scheduled without jeopardizing the analysis deadline.
rius.rationale: The prompt asks for prioritization of all three tasks.

rius.description: Avoid inventing unsupported urgency; acknowledge that exact ordering of the two shorter tasks can depend on current time or hidden constraints.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if the response does not fabricate a deadline for the other tasks and notes the missing context when relevant.
rius.rationale: Only one explicit clock deadline is provided.

task_objective: Design a prioritization method for five requests with only two staff available, using urgency, impact, dependencies, and effort.
constraints: Produce a method that can allocate scarce staff, not just a descriptive list.

rius.description: Evaluate urgency for each request using consistent criteria such as deadlines or time sensitivity.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if urgency is an explicit scoring/ranking factor.
rius.rationale: Urgency is explicitly required.

rius.description: Evaluate impact, including severity, number of affected users, or business consequence.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if impact is explicitly scored or compared.
rius.rationale: Impact is explicitly required.

rius.description: Account for dependencies or blocking relationships among requests.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if tasks that unblock others or depend on prerequisites affect ranking.
rius.rationale: Dependencies are explicitly required.

rius.description: Account for effort/capacity so the two available staff can feasibly execute the selected work.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if estimated effort influences assignment or order.
rius.rationale: Effort is explicitly required.

rius.description: Use a transparent scoring/triage method, assign the two staff, and revisit priorities as conditions change.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if the factors are converted into an actionable allocation and review process.
rius.rationale: A method should support actual resource assignment.

task_objective: Propose a fair way to prioritize support tickets when some affect an executive, some affect many students, and some have waited longest.
constraints: Do not prioritize solely by stakeholder status.
Include a mechanism that prevents old tickets from starving indefinitely.

rius.description: Rank severity/operational impact and number of affected users as core priority factors.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if broad impact and severity materially affect ticket rank.
rius.rationale: Many-user impact can outweigh requester prominence.

rius.description: Avoid automatically prioritizing a ticket solely because it affects an executive.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if stakeholder status is not treated as a trump card and is justified only through actual impact/urgency.
rius.rationale: The task asks for fairness across affected groups.

rius.description: Include ticket age, SLA, or an aging mechanism so long-waiting cases gain priority over time.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if waiting time has a defined role rather than being ignored.
rius.rationale: The prompt explicitly contrasts long-waiting tickets with other priorities.

rius.description: Use a transparent scoring/triage rule with documented exceptions for genuine emergencies.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if the approach is reproducible and exceptions require reasons.
rius.rationale: Transparency makes the process defensibly fair.

rius.description: Reassess the queue periodically as impact, outages, deadlines, or available information change.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if priorities are dynamic rather than permanently fixed.
rius.rationale: Support conditions can change.

task_objective: Create a decision process for conflicting requests from sales, support, engineering, and existing customers that prevents the loudest stakeholder from automatically winning.
constraints: Document why a request is selected or deferred.

rius.description: Define common decision criteria such as customer/user impact, strategic value, risk, urgency, effort, technical dependency, and evidence quality.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if requests are judged on shared criteria rather than stakeholder influence.
rius.rationale: Comparable criteria reduce political dominance.

rius.description: Require each stakeholder to provide evidence in a common format, such as affected users, revenue/risk data, incident frequency, or engineering constraints.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if claims are normalized into comparable evidence.
rius.rationale: Loudness should not substitute for evidence.

rius.description: Apply agreed weights/scoring or a structured deliberation process consistently across all requests.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if the response describes a repeatable ranking mechanism.
rius.rationale: A transparent mechanism is the core safeguard.

rius.description: Separate decision authority/governance from advocacy and document conflicts, trade-offs, and final rationale.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if the chosen request is justified against alternatives and unilateral stakeholder override is prevented.
rius.rationale: This directly addresses the loudest-stakeholder problem.

rius.description: Revisit deferred requests when evidence, capacity, or strategy changes.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if the process includes a review or reprioritization point.
rius.rationale: Conflicting requests may become valid later.

task_objective: Rank replacement needs across aging university systems using operational criticality, failure likelihood, security exposure, supportability, and migration complexity.
constraints: Treat migration complexity as a planning/risk factor rather than automatically rewarding easy projects.

rius.description: Assess operational criticality, including essential services and consequences of outage.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if criticality materially affects ranking.
rius.rationale: Operational criticality is explicitly required.

rius.description: Assess likelihood/indicators of failure using age, incidents, condition, or reliability evidence.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if failure probability or evidence is included.
rius.rationale: Failure likelihood is explicitly required.

rius.description: Assess security exposure, including vulnerabilities, unsupported components, or compensating-control gaps.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if security risk materially affects ranking.
rius.rationale: Security exposure is explicitly required.

rius.description: Assess supportability, including vendor support, available expertise, parts/patches, and maintainability.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if supportability materially affects ranking.
rius.rationale: Supportability is explicitly required.

rius.description: Assess migration complexity/dependencies and use it to sequence or mitigate replacement.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if migration difficulty/dependencies affect the roadmap.
rius.rationale: Migration complexity is explicitly required.

rius.description: Combine the factors into a documented risk-based portfolio and identify interim mitigations for high-risk systems that cannot yet be replaced.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if the framework produces an actionable phased replacement plan.
rius.rationale: Not all systems can be replaced at once.
